ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: ways to play
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Fourteen storytellers named for what they do, how a storyteller works and keeps every kind of event, and the story direction that leans any storyteller toward one of them.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Pick the way for a new game; change the direction any time in a game already running.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
Rimfolk adds fourteen storytellers to the game's storyteller screen. None of them is a character: each is a way to play, named for what it does, with a plain plate for its picture. Each is a whole storyteller with the game's own difficulty settings and the game's own endgame and DLC parts, and each leans Rimfolk's own happenings its way: its visitors, joiners, animals, finds, feasts, performers, camps, letters, favours asked, calls to arms, missions, world events, friends in a fight, omens and who a raid comes from.
The first eight shape the year in their own ways. The Long Road, Neighbours and Crossroads bring nothing less often than the base game does. Lean Years, Old Powers and What You Sow bring some things less often where that is what the way is about (fewer traders in lean years, fewer fights where the danger is strange, fewer friends for a cruel colony), and The Turning Year and Rise and Fall have quiet seasons and quiet times in their arcs; each one's description says what comes less often. The six added after them (Open Gate, Home and Hearth, The Wilds, Windfalls, Sellswords and Feast Days) only bring more of their own kind of thing: nothing comes less often than in the base game, nothing in them runs longer than a season, and their threats come on the classic cycle.
The story direction (Rimfolk's settings, What's on) leans whichever storyteller you play toward one of the fourteen, through Rimfolk's own happenings and the reasons raids come for. The storyteller keeps its own pace of threats and sickness and its own parts. With one of Rimfolk's as your storyteller, it plays its own way unless a direction is chosen; a direction chosen is the one that leans.

li.heading: How a storyteller works
li.text:
A storyteller is a set of parts, and each part is a clock for one kind of event. One part sends the big threats on a cycle: the classic storyteller's (Cassandra's) has about 4.6 days in which threats may come, then about 6 quiet ones. Other parts send the home's everyday happenings about every 5 days, traders and visitors a few times a year, sickness as the land brings it, quests, ship chunks, and help from allies when the colony is in danger. When a part's clock comes round, it draws one event of its kind from every event the game, the DLCs and your mods have put in that kind, each by its own chance and only if it can happen now. A storyteller never needs to know an event by name: a mod's new event joins its kind and comes with it. The difficulty settings decide how hard threats hit and how much else there is.
A way to play is such a storyteller with its parts tuned to what it is about, a few parts of Rimfolk's own where the game's can't say it (threats by the season or the arc, named events and quests, the omen of a trouble), and levers on Rimfolk's own happenings.

li.heading: How every kind of event keeps its chance

points.li: Every way is built on the game's own base storyteller, so the endgame, the DLCs' quests, the deep drill's insects, the anima and polux trees, Gauranlen pods and the monolith come as with any storyteller.

Every kind of event in the game and your mods has a part in every way. Rimfolk's tests read your mod list and fail if a kind has no part. The rarer kinds keep long clocks of their own: the other arrivals of peoples about every 25 days, orbital visitors about every 40, and the Settlers' protection fee about every 60.
No way shuts anything out: no part forbids an event, a kind or a place, except the raid beacon's own map, which keeps its own raids as it does under the game's storytellers.

Rimfolk's levers touch only Rimfolk's own happenings, and never take one below a quarter of its own rate or above three times it. A way takes something below the game's own rate only where that is what the way is about, and its description says so; the six added last take nothing below it at all.

Harm keeps the game's own rate. A lever on something that hurts is never above 1; over a year or an arc each way's threats come at the classic pace or less and its sickness about as often as the game's own; Rimfolk's everyday hurts stay within the same budget, a way only moving them between kinds.

A raid aimed by reason (Neighbours, What You Sow, Rise and Fall, Crossroads) only chooses which people comes, never how many raids, and never more than 85% of them: the rest are the game's own choice, so every people can still come.
The ways shaped by the season, the colony's deeds or the long arc move their levers about within the same floor and ceiling.

table.li: Way | How it plays | Raids against the classic pace | Rimfolk leans toward

Neighbours | The peoples around are the story | The classic pace, most from a people with a reason | Visitors, letters, favours, friends in a fight, peoples remembering
The Turning Year | The calendar decides, the same shape each year | About the same over a year: quiet springs, hard winters | Camps and trade in autumn, letters in winter, the season's world events
What You Sow | The colony's deeds decide | The classic pace; who comes is the deeds' | Traders, visitors and friends and fewer fights for kindness; fewer of them for cruelty; peoples remembering more
Old Powers | The world feels watched | Nearly the classic pace, stranger threats making up the rest | Omens, strange nights, the land and sky, pilgrims and seers, strange skies; fewer fights
Lean Years | Scarcity is the enemy | The classic pace | Fewer traders, visitors, camps and fights; blights, cold and heat; famine and drought in the region's word

Rise and Fall | A year of growth, then a year of trouble: the trouble foretold, the trouble, the rebuilding | About the same over the two years | Plenty and fewer fights in the year of growth, the trouble's own news, friends in the rebuilding
Crossroads | The colony as a market | The classic pace, larger raids as it grows rich | Traders, camps, visitors, favours and debts; rivals with a grudge
Open Gate | More people come to join | The classic cycle | Wanderers, refugees, escape pods, wild people and guests who stay; Rimfolk's events in which someone may join; visitors
Home and Hearth | The colonists' own lives | The classic cycle | Personal stories, pasts catching up, challenges, wagers, feasts and games

li.heading: The Long Road
li.text: Raids come to the gate on the classic cycle. Caravans meet the land's happenings as with any storyteller, and more besides: a chance meeting about every 6 days on the road and a small threat about every 12. Quests come a little more often, and traders, visitors and travellers come 6, 5 and 9 times a year instead of 5, 4 and 6. Rimfolk's letters from the region's notables come 1.6 times as often, so do favours called in and missions offered, camps 1.5 times, its traders and visitors 1.2 times, world events a little sooner, and the region's word leans to roads, towns, rushes and tolls. Nothing comes less often than in the base game.

li.heading: Neighbours
li.text: Most raids the storyteller sends without saying from whom come from the hostile people with the most reason: the wrongs the colony did them as they remember them, an old enmity, a cold goodwill. The raid's letter names the old wrong. With no people that has reason enough, the game chooses as ever, and a share of the raids always does. Allies send fighters more often when the colony is in danger, and Rimfolk's friends in a fight come 1.8 times as often. Letters, favours called in, a people's call to arms, traders and visitors come more often, the peoples remember a quarter more strongly, and the region's word leans to feuds, wars, courts and peace talks. Rimfolk's events that can end in a fight (revenge, debts called in, tribute, an old enemy) come at the game's own rate, since they are this way's own story: nothing comes less often than in the base game.

li.heading: The Turning Year
li.text: Threats come by the season: about a third of their peak in spring, half in summer, three quarters in autumn, all of it in winter. Sickness comes with the thaw, more than twice as often in spring and less the rest of the year. Traders come mostly in autumn and visitors in summer. Each season has its own happenings: herds on the move and floods in spring, heat waves and blight in summer, cold snaps and auroras in winter, and from your mods crops sprouting in spring, droughts, wildfires and weeds in summer and a whiteout in winter (Vanilla Events Expanded, Seasonal Weather, Vanilla Plants Expanded - Flowers). Rimfolk's camps come with the good weather and stay away in deep winter, letters come by the winter fire, fights from Rimfolk's events are hardest in late winter and fewest in spring, and the region's word follows the year: floods and herds, fairs, the harvest, the hard winter. Over a year each of these comes about as often as in the base game: what is missing in one season comes in another.

li.heading: What You Sow
li.text: The colony's deeds are what the peoples remember of it: the good turns it did them against the wrongs. A colony nobody remembers anything of is in the middle. Raids come at the classic pace whatever it does; the crueller it is, the more of them come from a people it wronged. Traders, visitors and friends in a fight come by the deeds: as in the base game for a colony nobody remembers anything of (about 5 traders and 4 visitors a year, and the classic storyteller's friends in a fight), up to 8 traders and 7 visitors for a kind colony, and down to a quarter of a kind colony's number for a cruel one. Rimfolk's visitors, traders, camps, letters, favours, missions and friends in a fight lean the same way. Kindness also spares the colony some trouble: Rimfolk's events that can end in a fight come down to 0.6 times as often and schemes against it to 0.4 times; for a cruel colony they come as in the base game, never more. The peoples remember everything 1.4 times as strongly. Nothing is told: the world simply answers.

li.heading: Old Powers
li.text: Raids nearly at the classic pace, and stranger threats making up the rest about every 40 days: psychic drones, maddened herds, things in the earth, a psychic storm (Vanilla Races Expanded - Archon), and the void's own where its content is on. Omens and strange nights about every 8 days: eclipses, auroras, a psychic calm, ambrosia, thrumbos passing, a meteorite, glowing spores, and from your mods a psychic hum, a meteor shower, a long night, a psychic bloom (Vanilla Events Expanded) or a mana surge and storm (A RimWorld of Magic). The home's everyday happenings come about every 6 days instead of 5, the omens taking their place. Rimfolk's events that can end in a fight (debt collectors, a war band, an old enemy's revenge) come 0.7 times as often: the danger here is strange rather than other people. Pilgrims and seers come more often, and so do blessings and gifts no one can explain; the land and the sky stir more in Rimfolk's events, the past catches up a little more, and the region's word leans to strange skies, comets, faith and wrecks. Rimfolk's own strange happenings come about twice as often, about one in ten days at a home against one in three weeks under any other way: a seer at the end of a season, a night when everyone awake turns to face one way, a stone that hums in a storm, a sealed scroll in old ruins, casters lit up under a sky full of power, a wandering enchanter, something knocking under the ground, the dead walking a road at dusk, pilgrims passing, another sky at night, an animal that speaks, signs of something going by in the night, pale wolves under the full moon, eyes at the edge of the dark. Each needs a reason, none comes within four days of another, and what hurts in them is rare and shown. It leans the world toward the uncanny and names nothing.

li.heading: Lean Years
li.text: Raids come at the classic pace, and a hardship about every 7 days: blight most of all, cold snaps and heat waves, storms, solar flares, alphabeavers, now and then a toxic fallout or a volcanic winter, and from your mods droughts, weeds in the fields, wildfires, acid rain, now and then a scorch or a whiteout (Vanilla Events Expanded, Vanilla Plants Expanded - Flowers, Seasonal Weather, Alpha Biomes). Fewer people come by: traders 2.5 times a year instead of 5, visitors 3 instead of 4 and travellers 5 instead of 6, orbital traders about two thirds as often, Rimfolk's trading camps and market caravans half as often, and its other camps and visitors 0.8 times as often. The home's everyday happenings (cargo pods, wanderers and the like) come about every 7 days instead of 5, with the hardships between them. Rimfolk's events that can end in a fight (debt collectors, a war band, an old enemy's revenge) come 0.7 times as often: the danger is the land more than other people. The region's word leans to famine, drought, scarcity, sickness and hard winters, and the everyday hurts Rimfolk adds lean to the cold, the hungry and the sick, within the same budget.

li.heading: Rise and Fall
li.text: An arc lasts two years: a year of rise, then a year of fall. The first year, all 60 of its days, is growth: raids come a little less often than at the classic pace, Rimfolk's events that can end in a fight and schemes against the colony less often, and traders, visitors and camps come in plenty. The second year begins with the omens: a few days in, the region's word of the coming trouble comes as one of Rimfolk's world events (a war, a plague, a famine, a hard winter or a strange sky), set by the world and never the same as the last arc's. 20 days into the year the trouble itself comes, for 20 days: the war's raids, the plague's sickness, the famine's blights (and droughts and weeds with your mods), the winter's cold snaps (and a whiteout), the sky's darkness (a long night, a psychic hum). While it lasts few traders, visitors or camps come, the region's other news comes a little less often, and Rimfolk's events that can end in a fight come more often. The year ends with 20 days of rebuilding, quiet, with traders coming back and friends more likely at hand, and then the next arc begins. Friends in a fight come at least as often as under the classic storyteller all through the arc. Over the two years threats and sickness come about as often as at the classic pace, traders and visitors more often, and Rimfolk's events that can end in a fight a little less often. Personal stories begin a little more often.

li.heading: Crossroads
li.text: Traders come 12 times a year, orbital traders about one and a half times as often, visitors and travellers more often, and Rimfolk's trading camps and market caravans twice as often. Raids come at the classic pace, larger as the colony grows rich, and about a third of them come from rivals with a grudge. Favours and debts, letters, camps and missions come more often, and the region's word leans to fairs, trade, roads, rushes and tolls. Nothing comes less often than in the base game.

li.heading: Open Gate
li.text: About every 10 days someone comes to join, on top of the game's own: a wanderer asking to join, a refugee in a crashed transport pod, a wild person wandering in, and from your mods a group of wild people (Vanilla Events Expanded), an escape pod (Vanilla Gravship Expanded) or a happy guest asking to stay for good (Hospitality). About every 20 days the game offers guests who ask to stay a while and may join at the end, refugees to shelter for a time (Royalty) or a downed refugee to rescue. How many come follows the storyteller's own sense of how big the colony should be, so a large colony sees fewer. Visitors come 6 times a year instead of 4, Rimfolk's visitors 1.3 times as often, and Rimfolk's events in which someone may join 2.5 times as often: a quiet stranger, a wounded stranger, a would-be apprentice, runaway lovers, an old comrade. Raids, sickness and everything else come as in the base game.

li.heading: Home and Hearth
li.text: Personal stories begin about twice as often (no more of them at once than usual), and Rimfolk's events in which a colonist's past catches up with them come about twice as often. Rimfolk's challenges come 1.6 times as often, and its feasts, fairs, games and wagers twice as often: a feast at a camp's fire, a harvest fair, a game for a stake, a travelling gambler, a wedding at the colony, a fair on the frozen river, the longest night kept awake, a neighbour's great day, a town's day. The steward thinks of holding a feast with guests twice as readily (still once a season at most, with offices on). Raids, sickness and everything else come as in the base game.

li.heading: The Wilds
li.text: About every 6 days one of the land's animal events comes, on top of the game's own: a herd passing through, thrumbos passing, farm animals wandering in, an animal that tames itself, ambrosia sprouting, and from your mods caravan and battle animals wandering in and wild crops sprouting (Vanilla Events Expanded), a behemoth passing (Alpha Animals), animals thought extinct passing (Vanilla Animals Expanded - Endangered), and herds and young of Pokémon (PokéWorld). Rimfolk's events of animals and great beasts come 2.5 times as often (a great beast on the land, a strange creature, orphaned young, the herd crossing, a tamer's challenge, the animal doctor), its events of the land and the sky 1.8 times, and the colonists' moments with their own animals and calm wild ones 2.5 times. The region's word leans to great herds, drove seasons and the old thrumbo. Predators, maddened animals, raids and everything else come as in the base game.

li.heading: Windfalls
li.text: About every 8 days something falls from the sky, on top of the game's own: cargo pods most of all, ship chunks, a meteorite, and from your mods pods of clothes and of weapons (Vanilla Events Expanded). About every 15 days the game offers something to explore as one of its quests: an item stash, an ancient complex (Ideology), an abandoned base (Real Ruins), a gravship's wreckage and stashes and wrecks in orbit (Odyssey); now and then a lost city (Go Explore) or untouched ruins (Real Ruins) are found. Rimfolk's finds and gifts come 2.5 times as often: treasure maps, buried caches, sealed crates, a door in the hill, lost cargo, a crashed drone, a fallen star, a child's or a pet's find, a wild harvest, an inheritance, and gifts from allies and old friends the colony once helped. The region's word leans to wrecks and opened vaults. Raids come as in the base game, and still grow with the colony's wealth.

li.heading: Sellswords
li.text: About every 15 days the game offers a fight for others as one of its quests: a bandit camp to clear, an ally's mission against one (Royalty), and from your mods an outlaw wanted for a bounty (Vanilla Factions Expanded - Settlers), a skirmish or a siege camp (Vanilla Factions Expanded - Medieval 2), an arcane bandits' camp (A RimWorld of Magic) or a deserters' hideout (Vanilla Factions Expanded - Empire); now and then a prison camp to free (Go Explore). A people's call to arms, when their town is attacked, comes 2.5 times as readily, and Rimfolk's events of champions, bounties and sellswords 2.5 times as often: a travelling champion and a rematch, a prisoner a people will pay for, a sellsword squad offering to hold the walls, a call to serve a season, a company's muster. The region's word leans to sellsword companies looking for work. Raids on the colony come as in the base game.

li.heading: Feast Days
li.text: Rimfolk's feasts, fairs, games and wagers come 2.5 times as often, and the steward thinks of holding a feast with guests 2.5 times as readily. Performers and storytellers come 2.5 times as often: a travelling storyteller, travelling players, a fiddler, a spirit-singer, a fortune teller, a play about the colony. The region's word leans to great fairs, moots of the peoples, bumper harvests and seasons of songs. Raids, sickness and everything else come as in the base game.

points.li: A new game: pick the way on the storyteller screen, with any difficulty.
A game already running: the game's options, Gameplay, Change storyteller. The new way leans from that moment.

The story direction: Rimfolk's settings, What's on, Story direction. It leans from that moment, over any storyteller, and none takes it off. A direction brings a way's levers on Rimfolk's happenings, its world events and its raids' reasons; a way's own parts (its named events and quests, its threats by the season or the arc) come only with the way as your storyteller.
What a way leans needs its part of Rimfolk switched on: camps, letters, world events, the gods, offices for the steward's feasts. A part switched off stays off.
